edit.description: the kill helper returns only once the pid it signalled is gone, so both signalled-run teardowns and the two reaping hooks remove a tree no live writer holds

summary: The signalled-run teardowns SIGKILL and remove in one breath, so `rm` walks the scratch repo under a writer still exiting and an ENOTEMPTY reds whichever case ran it
acceptance: a signalled-run teardown removes its scratch tree only after every pid it signalled is observably gone, so no cleanup races a live writer into an ENOTEMPTY attributed to the case that happened to run it
notes: Verified off run 36066310772's log: the red is `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '<scratch>/.flume'` from the case's `finally`, not an assertion — the case already waits on its line through `waitFor`, so the record's timing diagnosis does not hold. `killIfAlive` (`tests/cli.test.ts:2337`) signals and returns; both helpers (`:2893`, `:2405`) then `rm` recursively. No `tests[]`: a race's absence is not decidably red — the named exception in *A fix ships the test that would have caught it*.
